strengths: Novel and highly intuitive formulation: Reframing GUI grounding as an interactive, multi-step search task mimics human visual feedback loops and helps resolve the brittle spatial semantic alignment of static, one-step methods.

Strong empirical performance: Achieves state-of-the-art results on ScreenSpot-v2 (93.9%) and ScreenSpot-Pro (56.5%), notably outperforming prior methods like GTA1 on challenging, high-resolution UI layouts.

Rigorous reward and trajectory design: The proposed trajectory penalties (e.g., false stop, false direction, repeated position) are well-justified, and ablation studies clearly demonstrate how they prevent degenerate policy behaviors.

Insightful probing analysis: The 'cursor-in-box' test isolates and proves that the model develops a more robust spatial understanding and significantly reduces the strong positional center bias inherent in the base VLM (Qwen-2.5-VL-7B).
Excellent presentation: The manuscript is exceptionally well-written, features clear diagrams explaining the workflow, and provides detailed training dynamics and qualitative case studies.
weaknesses: Inference latency and cost: Multi-step interactive search requires generating long chain-of-thought ('thinking') tokens and processing multiple screenshots sequentially, which is significantly slower and more computationally expensive than single-step baseline predictors.

Sensitivity to initial crop in CCF: If the initial coarse prediction is inaccurate, the subsequent cursor-centric focusing crop may entirely miss the target UI element. The authors note this occurs in 10.3% of ScreenSpot-Pro cases, but a robust recovery or multi-scale zooming mechanism is currently missing.
High training complexity: Training with online GRPO over multi-step rollouts is computationally demanding and requires complex environment rendering, requiring 8x A100 GPUs for a 7B model.

strengths: Novel and intuitive reformulation of GUI grounding as an interactive, cursor-driven search process. Providing visual feedback of the cursor's location directly on the image successfully addresses the long-standing 'spatial semantic alignment' bottleneck of VLMs.

Outstanding empirical performance, establishing new state-of-the-art results on ScreenSpot-v2 (93.9%) and the highly challenging ScreenSpot-Pro (56.5%), outperforming existing supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning baselines.

Rigorous analysis and diagnostic experiments. The 'cursor-in-box' test is particularly insightful, exposing a severe center-position bias in the base Qwen-2.5-VL model and showing how the proposed RL framework implicitly improves general spatial reasoning.

Well-designed Cursor-Centric Focusing (CCF) strategy, which enables high-resolution target search on complex layouts while keeping training computationally lightweight by using downscaled screenshots.
Thorough ablation studies showing the clear necessity of each individual trajectory penalty (e.g., false stop, repeated position) and the spatial thinking tokens in preventing model degeneracy.
weaknesses: Increased inference latency: Multi-turn generation with detailed chain-of-thought ('think') tokens naturally increases time-to-first-token, execution latency, and overall API/GPU cost compared to fast, single-step coordinate predictors. The paper lacks a quantitative analysis/breakdown of average inference time per query.

Susceptibility to initial crop failures: Because the CCF strategy relies entirely on a crop around the first-step coordinate, if the initial prediction is completely off (which happens in ~10% of ScreenSpot-Pro cases), the target element is excluded from the search field, leaving the model with no path to recovery.

Lack of end-to-end evaluation: While the improvements on pure grounding benchmarks are clear, evaluating how the improved grounding accuracy translates to complete execution success in full agent benchmarks (e.g., Mind2Web or OSWorld) would strengthen the practical significance of the work.

strengths: An interesting reformulation of the GUI grounding task as an interactive, multi-step search using a virtual cursor to provide explicit visual feedback.
Comprehensive trajectory-based reward design (such as penalties for false stops, repeated positions, and false directions) to regularize reinforcement learning.
The 'cursor-in-box' probing task is a clever, clean diagnostic experiment that highlights the spatial/positional biases of base VLMs.
Achieves strong results on the ScreenSpot-v2 and ScreenSpot-Pro benchmarks, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods when using the proposed inference strategy.
weaknesses: The core reinforcement learning framework heavily relies on a simple heuristic—Cursor-Centric Focusing (CCF)—to beat the state-of-the-art. As shown in Figure 2b, without CCF, GUI-CURSOR's performance drops to 45.3% on ScreenSpot-Pro, which is lower than the baseline GTA1 model (50.1%). This indicates that the interactive RL framework alone does not outperform existing one-step baselines.

High inference latency and computational overhead. Multi-turn autoregressive visual-language generation (especially with dense `<think>` tokens and high-resolution screenshots) is highly impractical for real-time GUI agents, which need to run grounding steps continuously.

The Cursor-Centric Focusing (CCF) strategy introduces a major error propagation issue. If the initial coordinate prediction is off, the target element will be cropped out of the frame. The paper acknowledges this hard limitation, noting that 10.3% of ScreenSpot-Pro cases suffer from this failure mode.

Training complexity is disproportionately high. Fine-tuning a 7B parameter VLM using multi-step trajectory rollouts with GRPO requires substantial resource overhead (8 x A100 GPUs) for a behavior that, as analyzed, collapses to a single-step or two-step decision for 95% of the test instances.

Lack of comparison to simpler iterative baselines. The paper does not evaluate whether a model trained using simple multi-step Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with cursor rendering could achieve similar performance without the complexity of GRPO and dense trajectory rewards.

strengths: Reframing GUI grounding as an interactive search with a virtual cursor is a highly intuitive and effective paradigm that mimics human trial-and-error behavior.

Outstanding empirical results, notably outperforming state-of-the-art models like GTA1 on challenging benchmarks (e.g., +8.0% improvement on ScreenSpot-Pro) while being highly data-efficient (requiring only 8K training samples compared to GTA1's 64K).

Thorough and insightful analysis of spatial reasoning capabilities, including a custom-designed diagnostic 'cursor-in-box' test which clearly highlights the spatial limitations of standard VLMs and how the proposed method mitigates them.
Comprehensive ablation studies demonstrating the necessity of each proposed trajectory penalty and the importance of reasoning/thinking tokens.
The Cursor-Centric Focusing (CCF) strategy represents a practical and elegant way to manage the computational cost of high-resolution multi-step reasoning.
weaknesses: Multi-step inference naturally incurs higher latency compared to single-step models. Although the trade-off is favorable on difficult datasets, it could be a limitation in real-time latency-sensitive applications.

The Cursor-Centric Focusing (CCF) strategy can fail to recover when the initial coarse prediction is very far from the target (as acknowledged in Section J, where the target is cropped out in ~10.3% of ScreenSpot-Pro cases), and the model currently lacks a robust mechanism to zoom out or re-center.

Implementing the proposed method requires an active rendering wrapper during both training and inference to display the cursor on the screen, adding slight environmental and pipeline complexity compared to simple coordinate-outputting models.

strengths: Reframes GUI visual grounding as an interactive cursor-movement search task, providing a natural visual feedback loop that helps the model align predicted coordinates with actual on-screen positions.

Leverages multi-step online Reinforcement Learning (via GRPO) with well-formulated trajectory penalties (such as false stop and repeated position penalties) to effectively regularize the search policy and prevent degenerate behaviors.

Achieves state-of-the-art results on several challenging benchmarks (e.g., ScreenSpot-Pro, UI-Vision) while being exceptionally data-efficient, requiring only 8K training samples compared to 64K for prior leading methods.

Outlines a simple and effective Cursor-Centric Focusing (CCF) strategy that crops the screenshot during inference, allowing the model to perform fine-grained coordinate correction without the heavy computational burden of high-resolution training.

Deeply analyzes the spatial reasoning capability of the model through a customized 'cursor-in-box' probing task and out-of-distribution spatial benchmarks, demonstrating that interactive RL training genuinely improves the model's fundamental spatial reasoning.
weaknesses: The multi-step visual feedback loop inherently introduces additional computational latency and throughput overhead at inference time compared to standard one-step coordinate prediction methods.

The Cursor-Centric Focusing (CCF) module is highly dependent on the quality of the initial step's prediction. If the first coarse prediction is too far from the target, the element gets cropped out, and the model currently lacks a mechanism to dynamically zoom out or re-center.
Currently restricted to point-click actions; extensions to more complex, continuous GUI interactions (like drag-and-drop or scrolling) are discussed conceptually but not empirically validated.

strengths: Innovative Reframing of Grounding: Reframing GUI grounding as an interactive search with a virtual cursor is a highly intuitive idea. It provides valuable visual feedback that helps the VLM align continuous pixel coordinates with discrete token representations.

Remarkable Data Efficiency: GUI-CURSOR achieves superior accuracy compared to established baselines on ScreenSpot-Pro (e.g., outperforming GTA1-7B by a significant margin) while utilizing only 8K training samples compared to the baseline's 64K samples.
Thorough Diagnostic Probing: The inclusion of the 'cursor-in-box' test is a clever way to isolate and evaluate the core spatial reasoning limits of VLMs independently of complex GUI contextual cues.

Detailed Empirical Analysis: The paper provides extensive analyses, including detailed training dynamics, ablation studies on trajectory rewards/penalties, and generalizability to out-of-distribution benchmarks.
weaknesses: High Training and Inference Latency: Reframing a one-step coordinate prediction into a multi-step interactive search significantly increases the computational footprint. During GRPO training, trajectory rollouts act as a major bottleneck, more than doubling the training time per step. At inference, throughput decreases by up to 41% when executing more steps.

Vulnerability to Initial Predictions in CCF: The Cursor-Centric Focusing (CCF) strategy relies entirely on the correctness of the initial step's coarse prediction. If this prediction is inaccurate, the target element is cropped out (which occurs in 10.3% of ScreenSpot-Pro cases). The model currently lacks a robust mechanism to zoom out or recover from this out-of-crop failure mode.

Visual Occlusion of Small Targets: Rendering a virtual cursor onto the screen introduces a physical hazard where the cursor can entirely occlude small target elements (e.g., a 10x10 close button) at the final step, limiting the model's fine-grained visual verification.

Scope Limited to Click-Style Grounding: The evaluation and design focus exclusively on point-and-click interactions. Continuous GUI interactions, such as dragging, sliding, and scrolling, are left to future work, limiting the method's immediate readiness for generalist GUI agent environments.
